Brigitte Nielsen: From 80s Action Queen to Reality TV Icon

In 1985, towering Danish beauty Brigitte Nielsen burst onto Hollywood screens as the sword-wielding warrior in Red Sonja. From her whirlwind marriage to Sylvester Stallone to reality TV fame with Flavor Flav to becoming a mom again at 54 - discover the Amazon's incredible reinvention story.

Originally published 12 June 2025 · RewindZone Archive

1980sAction

The towering Danish beauty who dominated the decade - where is she today?

I still remember the first time I saw Brigitte Nielsen on screen. There she was, all 6 feet of Amazonian power, wielding a sword in Red Sonja like she was born for it. The 1980s belonged to larger-than-life action heroes, and Nielsen carved out her own legendary space among them.

The statuesque Danish actress exploded onto Hollywood's radar in 1985, becoming an instant icon of 80s cinema. From her warrior princess debut to her tumultuous marriage with Sylvester Stallone, Nielsen's story reads like pure Hollywood drama.

But what happened after the spotlight dimmed? How did the woman once dubbed "The Amazon" reinvent herself for a new generation? Let's dive into the fascinating journey of Brigitte Nielsen - from action star to reality TV queen to modern-day mother.

The THEN: Rise of an 80s Amazon (1985-1990)

Brigitte Nielsen - The Reluctant Supermodel Turned Action Star

Advertisement

THEN: At 22 years old in 1985, Nielsen was a Danish model who had worked with photography legends like Helmut Newton and Greg Gorman. Standing 6 feet 1 inch tall, she was a striking presence who caught producer Dino De Laurentiis' eye for a fantasy epic.

Her breakout role as the sword-wielding warrior in Red Sonja alongside Arnold Schwarzenegger launched her into instant stardom. The film showcased her unique combination of European elegance and fierce physicality. This wasn't just another pretty face - this was a woman who could hold her own next to Schwarzenegger himself.

NOW: At 61, Nielsen has come full circle with her relationship to her early fame. She embraced her action hero legacy when she returned to the Rocky franchise in Creed II (2018), reprising her role as Ludmilla Drago over 30 years later.

Her modeling background served her well - she walked the runway for Balenciaga's Fall 2024 fashion show in Los Angeles, proving that Amazon power never truly fades.

The Stallone Era: Hollywood's Power Couple

THEN: Nielsen's life changed forever when she met Sylvester Stallone during Red Sonja's promotional tour. Their whirlwind romance led to marriage in December 1985, making them one of Hollywood's most talked-about couples.

She starred opposite Stallone in Rocky IV (1985) as the cold, calculating Ludmilla Drago, wife of Ivan Drago. Her performance was understated but memorable - she brought an icy elegance that made the Soviet threat feel real.

Their collaboration continued with Cobra (1986), where Nielsen played a fashion model targeted by a cult. The film gave audiences a glimpse of the real-life chemistry between the newlyweds.

NOW: Despite their messy 1987 divorce, Nielsen and Stallone maintained a professional respect that allowed them to work together again in Creed II. Their scenes together crackle with the weight of shared history.

In recent interviews, Nielsen has spoken fondly of their time together, calling it a "learning experience" that shaped her understanding of Hollywood.

The Villain Era: Beverly Hills Cop II and Beyond

THEN: After her divorce from Stallone, Nielsen proved she could carry scenes on her own merit. Her role as Karla Fry in Beverly Hills Cop II (1987) showcased her as a formidable antagonist opposite Eddie Murphy.

At 24, she had already established herself as Hollywood's go-to European villain. Her height, accent, and commanding presence made her perfect for roles that required sophistication with an edge of danger.

The press dubbed her "The Amazon," a nickname that stuck throughout her career.

NOW: Nielsen looks back on this period as her "learning the craft" years. She's proud that she held her own against established stars like Murphy and Stallone while still developing her acting skills.

Her villain work established a template that influenced how tall, striking actresses would be cast in action films for years to come.

The EVOLUTION: From A-List to Reality (1990-2005)

European Success and Musical Ventures

Advertisement

After Hollywood's A-list phase, Nielsen didn't disappear - she evolved. She moved to Italy, where she found success hosting television shows and starring in the fantasy series Fantaghirò.

Her music career took off in unexpected ways. Her single "Body Next to Body" with Falco hit No. 6 in Austria and No. 22 in Germany. She recorded full albums, proving that her talents extended beyond action sequences.

This period taught her the value of reinvention - a skill that would serve her well in later decades.

The Reality TV Revolution

Nielsen's second act began in the early 2000s with reality television. Her appearance on The Surreal Life (2004) introduced her to a new generation who knew her more as a personality than an action star.

Her relationship with Flavor Flav became the stuff of reality TV legend. Their spin-off show Strange Love (2005) was essential viewing for anyone trying to understand early 2000s pop culture.

She didn't shy away from showing vulnerability, appearing on Celebrity Rehab with Dr. Drew in 2008 to address her struggles with alcoholism.

The NOW: Motherhood and Modern Fame (2006-Present)

Late-in-Life Love and Motherhood

Brigitte Nielsen found lasting love with Mattia Dessì, 15 years her junior, whom she married in 2006. Their relationship has endured for nearly two decades, proving that Nielsen finally found her perfect match.

In 2018, at age 54, Nielsen gave birth to daughter Frida after a long fertility journey. This late-in-life motherhood became a source of inspiration for women everywhere.

"Half the world was saying I was too old when I got pregnant at 54"

Nielsen has said. But she proved the doubters wrong, embracing motherhood with the same fearless attitude she brought to sword fighting.

Current Projects and Legacy

Now 61, Nielsen remains active across multiple platforms. She's a regular on social media, sharing glimpses of life with young Frida and maintaining connections with fans worldwide.

Her autobiography "You Only Get One Life" reached the Top 5 on Denmark's bestseller list, showing that audiences are still fascinated by her journey.

Recent appearances include reality shows across Europe and occasional acting roles. She's also become something of a fashion icon again, walking for major designers and proving that Amazon power never truly fades.

Current Status:

  • Married to Mattia Dessì since 2006
  • Mother to 6-year-old daughter Frida
  • Active on social media and European television
  • Estimated net worth: $10-12 million
  • Still modeling and making occasional film appearances

Film Legacy and Cultural Impact

Brigitte Nielsen's 1980s films hold up remarkably well today. Red Sonja has found new life as a cult classic, while Rocky IV remains one of the most beloved entries in the franchise.

Her return in Creed II felt like a triumphant homecoming. Seeing her reprise Ludmilla Drago reminded audiences why she made such an impact in the first place.

Critics have reassessed her work more favorably in recent years. What once seemed like simple action movie casting now looks like prescient recognition of her screen presence and physicality.

You Might Remember This If...

You witnessed the phenomenon of the "Amazon" actress in 1980s action cinema. Nielsen's height and presence paved the way for physically imposing women in action roles.

You remember when celebrity marriages were front-page news, and the Stallone-Nielsen union dominated tabloids for two years.

You caught Strange Love during VH1's reality TV golden age. Their relationship was bizarre, entertaining, and oddly touching.

You've ever wondered what happened to those larger-than-life 80s stars who seemed to disappear from mainstream Hollywood.

You believe that reinvention is possible at any age - Nielsen proved it multiple times throughout her career.

The Bottom Line

Brigitte Nielsen never played it safe. From leaving Denmark at 16 to pursue modeling, to diving headfirst into Hollywood's deep end, to reinventing herself through reality TV, she's always chosen the bold path.

Her story reflects something beautiful about the entertainment industry - that there's room for multiple acts in a single career. The woman who once wielded swords alongside Schwarzenegger found equal fulfillment as a reality TV star and late-in-life mother.

At 61, Nielsen continues to defy expectations. Whether she's walking fashion week runways or sharing parenting moments on Instagram, she approaches life with the same fearless energy that made her an 80s icon.

The Amazon never really left - she just found new territories to conquer.

What's your favorite Brigitte Nielsen era? Share your memories of the Danish Amazon in the comments below.
